window_caveat: Reference host dp sizes from existing harness/documents. Flip 360x880 is a narrow/tall reference, not a newly measured model resolution. Re-measure actual model/OS/dp/density and supported display states on SRTL.
implementation: CalendarTextFit/CalendarShiftLabel measure actual string width and normal line metrics with matching resolved style, locale, direction, weight and fixed text scaler. Height establishes common cap; only overflow reduces actual font. No name-length buckets.
Periwinkle uses the same height cap for a single cell and a joined weekly run; length affects width only. Existing week boundaries, run slicing and date touch targets remain.

CalendarCellMetrics reserves maximum three memo rows, date and Korean annotation before choosing chip height. Width growth is gentle, maximum 1.35 for stacked cells; split wide shift-band growth is separately capped at 1.15 after host visual review to avoid tall bands.

App-only AdaptiveCalendarCell preserves per-theme ordering/anchors: main central-date/bottom-memo stack, diary 35:65 header, grid date/annotation row, top soft-card group, initial circle and event four auxiliary slots. Old Korean bar functions retained byte-for-byte in this task.

Existing wide 40:60 date/annotation vs memo columns and Ultra two-line holiday annotations preserved. Global cells reserve no holiday/lunar slot, while Korean blanks retain one. Global holiday dates/detail-popup policy unchanged.

Memo sizes derive from common height cap, not the current shift name. Stacked and wide profiles use fixed sizes for 0..3 memos; long memos show complete grapheme prefixes without ellipsis or per-string font reduction.
Height/width fitting replaces layered whole-cell scaling on new paths. Existing Korean bar and excluded underline/editorial paths keep their previous behavior.
Metrics cache keys include actual cell size/theme/style/locale/Korean/wide/annotation lines; font-loading notifications invalidate cache. No model-name conditionals or old folded-width cache.
No public shared-web policy expansion; no language resource, P0/native alarm or release feature scope changes.
